subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 33-year-old woman participates in a study in which her cultured fibroblasts are irradiated during S phase. The resulting DNA double-strand breaks are repaired using the newly synthesized sister chromatid as a template, and the original sequence is restored without any loss of nucleotides.
question: Which of the following best describes the process responsible for this accurate repair?

options.text: It joins DNA ends without homology and frequently deletes nucleotides
It removes RNA primers and replaces them with DNA
It uses a complementary strand from an intact homologous duplex as a template to restore the sequence
It removes altered bases through a glycosylase and an AP site
It removes mismatched nucleotides from the newly synthesized strand

explanation_correct: Homologous recombination requires two homologous DNA duplexes and repairs a damaged strand using the complementary strand of an intact homolog as a template. This restores the duplex accurately without loss of nucleotides and is defective in breast and ovarian cancers with BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations and in some types of Fanconi anemia.

explanation_incorrect.A: That description applies to nonhomologous end joining, which is error-prone.
explanation_incorrect.B: Removal of RNA primers is part of DNA replication, not double-strand break repair.
explanation_incorrect.D: Glycosylase-mediated base removal is base excision repair.
explanation_incorrect.E: Removal of mismatched nucleotides is mismatch repair.

educationalObjective: Homologous recombination accurately repairs double-strand breaks by using an intact homologous duplex as a template.
